children: and S&P Dow Jones Indices (S&P DJI) have agreed to extend their exclusive licensing agreement by 25 years.
The deal extends Cboe's exclusive licensing rights for S&P 500 Index
options through 2051. The companies may also collaborate to pursue innovation beyond traditional index derivatives, including new products like tokenized options contracts.
The agreement builds on more than 40 years of collaboration between Cboe and S&P DJI that began in 1983 with the launch of SPX options.
CBOE shares jumped 6.6% premarket following the

Under the extended agreement, Cboe said there will be no change to its 2026 royalty fees, while revised terms will take effect in 2027. The company expects the 2027 fees to have a de minimis impact on net revenue growth, considering organic and ecosystem-driven volume growth, pricing opportunities, and continued business execution.

Cboe believes the extended contract, as structured, positions Cboe for growth, with future royalty fee adjustments smaller than the 2027 reset. The company plans to provide more specific 2027 organic total net revenue guidance in February alongside its fourth-quarter results.
